text:
A demand-paging system has 4 physical frames P 1 , P 2 , P 3 , P 4 .

The page-reference sequence is:

A ,   B ,   C ,   D ,   E ,   B ,   A ,   D ,   B ,   C

Initially, all frames are empty.

Two replacement policies are considered:

  1. LRU
     
  2. Clock

For Clock, on a page fault, advance the clock hand first and then inspect the use bit.

Which option correctly gives the final contents of frames P 1 , P 2 , P 3 , P 4 ?
options:
LRU: ( C , B , A , D )
Clock: ( E , B , A , C )

LRU: ( E , B , C , D )
Clock: ( C , B , A , D )

LRU: ( C , A , B , D )
Clock: ( E , C , A , B )

LRU: ( E , B , A , C )
Clock: ( C , B , A , D )

text:
A paged virtual-memory system has the following measured parameters:

\[
\begin{array}{|l|l|}
\hline
\textbf{Measurement} & \textbf{Value} \
\hline
P_t = \text{probability of a TLB miss} 
& 0.1 \
\hline

P_p = \text{probability of a page fault when a TLB miss occurs} 
& 0.0002 \
\hline

T_t = \text{time to access TLB} 
& 0 \
\hline

T_m = \text{time to access memory} 
& 1\ \text{microsecond} \
\hline

T_d = \text{time to transfer a page to/from disk} 
&
10   milliseconds = 10000   microseconds \
\hline

P_d = \text{probability page is dirty when replaced} 
& 0.5 \
\hline
\end{array}
\]

Additional assumptions:

  • The TLB is refilled automatically by hardware.
     
  • On a TLB miss, one memory access is required to read the page-table entry.
     
  • If a page fault occurs, the required page must be read from disk.
     
  • If the selected victim is dirty, it must also be written to disk.
     
  • Other page-replacement and page-table-update overheads are included in T d .
     

What is the average memory access time, in microseconds?

Suppose a 32 K × 8 K matrix A with 1 -byte elements is stored in row-major order in virtual memory.

Assume:

  • Only this program occupies physical memory.
     
  • The matrix begins exactly at a page boundary.
     
  • The matrix is initially on disk.
     
  • Demand paging is used.
     

The following code is executed:

for (i = 0; i < 32768; i++)
    for (j = 0; j < 8192; j++)
         A[i][j] = A[i][j] * A[i][j];

If execution of this code produces exactly 8 K page faults, what is the page size?
options: 4 KB
8 KB
16 KB

A virtual-memory system uses the LRU page-replacement algorithm.

There are four physical page frames at hexadecimal addresses:

4000 ,   5000 ,   6000 ,   7000

The page-reference sequence is:

1 → 2 → 3 → 4 → 2 → 5 → 3 → 1 → 6 → 5 → 4

For the initial references 1 , 2 , 3 , 4 , the pages are loaded as follows:

 Page Frame Address 1 4000 2 5000 3 6000 4 7000

At which address is page 4 loaded when it is referenced for the last time?
options: 4000
5000
6000

text: Which of the following statements about page-replacement policies are correct?
options: LRU always produces fewer page faults than FIFO.
OPT always performs at least as well as LRU.
For any replacement policy, increasing the number of available frames can never decrease the hit percentage.
With LRU, increasing the number of available frames cannot decrease the hit percentage.
Random replacement is always worse than LRU.
